_note: Frontier economy numbers (F2). F0.2 values approved by Tim 2026-11-02; everything else is a placeholder for Tim to tune. Time units: 'ticks' = economy ticks (1 per cadenceTicks sim ticks).

workers._note: placeholder, Tim to tune (L3.5/L3.6). tiers._note: Economy balance B3, placeholder, Tim to tune: town hall tiers (tier 1 first, set at founding). ring = build radius in world units from the hall for every zone, town building, wall and gate (roads and work camps may go outside); cells = most zoned cells per zone kind; placed = most of each placed building type (camps counts lumber_camp + quarry together); workers = most workers incl. training; upgrade = what moving UP to this tier costs (pop counts townspeople + workers) and how many economy ticks it takes.

upkeep._note: Economy balance B5, placeholder, Tim to tune: paid every economy tick. The first freeLevels grown zone levels of a town are free; above that, zones pay their rate per grown level (scaled by the share above the free allowance). Short zone upkeep lowers that zone's health (less output and housing; long shortages abandon it, then it recovers). buildings = per built placed building; lines = per wall (w) / gate (g) cell; workerWage = per worker incl. training (short wages show as waiting). goodsByStage = goods per housing cell at stage 1, 2, 3: housing levels up to stage 2+ only while goods are paid; short goods never lower a level, they cost goodsShortMood of mood.

war._note: Goals pass (Tim 2026-11-19), placeholders, Tim to tune: the 2nd town goals. pack = what the Pack for war goal asks the hero to carry (the bot war pack for a tier 1 town); defendCoffers = ryo the first town keeps in its coffers for its defenders' war chest.

F6 war, checkpoint 1 (Tim 2026-11-10), placeholders, Tim to tune. circleRadius = war circle round the target's town hall. Planting the war camp banner is the declaration: band = banner distance from the hall, the town's build ring + inner to + outer (widenStep = how far the outer edge widens at a time when no ground in the band can be built on, up to the circle); placeRange = most distance from the hero to the banner spot; campSpacing = least distance to another war camp banner; cooldownDays = game days after a war ends before anyone can declare on that town again; historyMax = ended wars kept in the save.

morale._note: Checkpoint 8a (Tim 2026-11-14), placeholders, Tim to tune. weights: what each building is worth on its side's morale bar; a type not listed does not count (walls, palisades, gates, supply tents, field clinic, gather camps). The bar is the weight still standing over the weight of every counted building that has stood during the war.

channel._note: Checkpoint 8a (Tim 2026-11-14), placeholders, Tim to tune: taking a hall. seconds = how long the hero channels at the ruined hall; reach = how near the edge of the ruin he must stand; moveCancel = how far he may shift before it breaks off. A hit starts the count again.

outcomes._note: Checkpoint 8a: sackShare = share of the town coffers a sack takes for the attacker's Clan treasury.

rout._note: Checkpoint 8a: when a war ends its troops run this far from the town over this many seconds, fading, then leave the map.

war._cooldownNote: Tim 2026-11-15: 3 game days after any war (was 6), and 3 after accepted terms (surrender.cooldownDays)

surrender._note: War checkpoint 8c (sim/frontier/war_terms.js), placeholders, Tim to tune. offerSeconds = how long an offer waits for an answer (then it counts as refused for good); gapSeconds = how long the surrendering side has to make its first or next offer; outcomeSeconds = how long the attacker has to choose capture, sack or burn after a defender left without terms (then the town is sacked); cooldownDays after accepted terms; noise = how far a clan's guess of its chance to win is off, either way. bot: answerSeconds before a bot answers or offers; it refuses for good after maxLow offers below its price; when it surrenders it raises its offer by raise each time, at most maxOffers; it only thinks of surrendering notBeforeSeconds into a war, every everySeconds, when its loss looks at least lossAt likely, and then by chance. worth (ryo): tier = a town's worth by hall tier; material = ryo a unit of timber, stone or goods counts for; building = share of a standing building's cost that counts; hero, crew = the fighting worth of a hero and a crew member (a war troop counts its price); town = each other town the clan is known to hold; business = each city business it holds; weight = each morale point still standing.

general._stockadeNote: 8d-9 (Tim 2026-11-16): stockade in a defend.build list = a town stockade (as many as the list names and the tier allows: Siege three, Raider one, Rush none); in an attack.build or fortify.build list = the camp stockade. Ranged troops (rangedUnits) go into a stockade with room before a house, in the town and at the camp (camp: while they are not on a push).
general._note: War checkpoint 8d (sim/frontier/war_general.js, sim/war_general_brain.js), placeholders, Tim to tune. The bot general runs a bot clan's side of a war always and a player's side while his hero is outside the war circle. reviewSeconds = how often it looks and gives orders; default = a player's strategy until he picks; keepShare = share of the town coffers a player's general leaves when it fills the defender's war chest (per town: warKeep); botKeepShare = the same for a bot clan; chestStep = least ryo it moves at a time; launchTownDays = a bot starts a war only from an own town founded at least this many game days ago (Tim 2026-11-15); maxAttacks = wars a bot clan attacks in at once. Defence (8d-2): queueAhead = troops it keeps waiting at each training building; rangedUnits go into houses; menders = workers it sends to each fire or damaged hall or military building (below mendBelow of its health), mendersMax in all; defendReach = how far outside the build ring it meets attackers; retarget = how far the enemy must move before troops are re-sent; the army waits holdAt of the ring from the hall toward the camp, within holdRadius; buildSeconds = how often a bot town looks at its defences; buildReserve = stock it keeps on top of a building's cost; it builds between buildClear and buildRadius cells from the hall. Attack (8d-3), attack: pack = what a bot's hero packs at its launch town (from that town's coffers and stock); keep = what the town must still have left; planSeconds = how often a bot at peace looks for a war; planDays = it gives a plan up after this long; sackedSkipDays = it leaves a sacked town alone this long after its truce; target score = (tier worth + pop x popWorth - built military buildings x fortPenalty) / (1 + distance / distanceScale). Camp: sites = building sites at once; resourceRange = how far from the camp hall it looks for trees and stone for a lumber camp or quarry; workerReserve = ryo kept when hiring workers; guard = it meets defenders this near the camp; rallyOut = the army gathers this far from the camp hall toward the town; engage = while pushing it turns on defenders this near; fallBack = share of pushAt at which a push is given up. 8d-8: roles = mix keys that stand for whatever this clan trains at the buildings listed (special, siege, rider); mixSlack = a training building waits while its best unit is this far (in held / weight) ahead of the unit the mix is shortest of; sallyEdge = the defending army in the field sallies at the camp when its troops are worth this many times (in ryo) the attacker troops it sees, comes home below sallyHold and rests sallyRest seconds; wall (bot towns in peace, strategies with defend.wall): the line runs inset cells inside the build ring, at least gates gates (gateGap cells apart) plus one at each road or rail crossing, step wall cells at a time, keeping reserve timber, looked at again after lookDays, a new tier or a war. attack.packByTier = the pack by the target town hall tier (a launch town must hold that pack and keep); attack.fortify = the camp digs in after afterSeconds of war, a push given up, or at least `least` defenders in sight worth edge times its own troops: it builds `build` first and the palisade line; a push is one wave (troops trained meanwhile gather at the camp), and after each push given up the next waits for regroup times more troops (regroupMost times at most, never more than the troop cap); gather = the share of camp gatherers the general keeps on timber (short = the share on a resource whose stock is under half of the other), one worker moved per look, at most perSpot on one spot, no spot further than far from the camp hall.
general._buildOnNote: sell = what a bot's defending town sells at the capital by train while its war chest is under war.supply.chestLow (what it can spare above the town's keep amounts, a trainload at a time, the best paying first). troopRyo = the ryo a general reckons per free troop place when it sizes a coffers order for its war chest. Tim 2026-11-17 (each side uses all it has): after its strategy's own build list (defend.build in a town, attack.build at a camp) a general goes on with supply tents up to their max and then buildOn, in order, on top of what its list names (a type at its max is skipped; a camp gets the hall upgrade one of them needs, a town only when it can pay it). A town at peace builds only the supply tents of this tail; the rest once a war is on it. Supply tents also come before the list while the side is at its troop cap with ryo to train more. The tail never holds a push back.

strategies._raidNote: Tim 2026-11-17 (Raider only, placeholders): defend.lineRaid = while the defenders are not strong enough to sortie, party troops (riders first) go out to break the war camp's supply line (the rail section nearest the town, else the camp station) while at least home stay at home, giving up after giveUpSeconds and resting restSeconds after each raid; attack.targets station = the town's railway station (a ruined station closes its lines).
strategies._note: Per strategy, defend: mix = the troop mix the town trains toward (roster units, weights; only what its buildings train); build = the military buildings a bot town puts up in this order, in peace and war (a type listed twice = two of it); sortieAt = troops out of houses before the defenders go for the war camp (they fall back at half of it). attack: build = the camp buildings in order; mix = troop mix; workers = camp workers it hires up to; pushAt = troops before the army pushes; targets = what the army goes for first (tower, workers, military, hall; military buildings and the hall always follow; walls and gates are broken only when no way leads in); palisade = a line of palisade between camp and town (out from the camp hall, length). 8d-8: mix and build may name roles (general.roles) and clan buildings (another clan skips them); upgrade in a build list = the town hall war upgrade; defend.wall.share = share of the ring a bot town walls (1 = all round, less = the side its roads leave by).

attack._temperNote: placeholders (Tim 2026-11-17): at war start a general is bold (odds: the strategy's attack.bold, else this) or patient. Patient builds its list before a full push (8d-10). Bold pushes in full once it has boldReady troops with that many ranged. Any general pushes early when its army is worth edgePush times the defenders it sees within scout of the town. Never into a town stockade before it has siege guns.

supply._note: placeholders (Tim 2026-11-17): a camp order no town has filled for buyAfterSeconds gets a capital-buy offer from the war chest (above war.supply.chestLow); stores beyond what the next planAhead buildings of the plan need (and the camp hall upgrade when one of them needs it), the low marks and buildReserve are sold at the capital, at least sellMin a sale

attack._armoryNote: 8e-9: general.armory.reserve = what the war chest and stock keep on top of an armory upgrade the general buys (it buys for the group it has most troops of, weapons then armor).
attack._supplyNote: 8e-7: a camp with a linked camp station: the general orders `order` timber (stone) by train from the clan's towns while camp stock is under timberLow (stoneLow), one open order each; a strategy may set its own (Raider leans on supply). camp_station in a build list is skipped while the clan has no town with a railway station.
attack._planNote: 8d-10 (Tim 2026-11-16): siegeUp = once the town it attacks has a stockade, the camp builds siegeUp.build right after the first barracks, lumber camp and quarry of its list (the foundry; the camp hall upgrade comes with it) and trains siege guns at least siegeUp.siege in its mix. While a building of its plan is not built the camp does not push in full: probes (a strategy may set its own) pushes at most, until buildWaitSeconds after the war began; training keeps back the ryo of the camp hall upgrade while the plan needs it.

pack._note: Pack for war (checkpoint 2): what the hero may carry to a war camp. max per resource, min = least amount if any is carried (0 = none needed). The pack is optional: a banner can be planted without one. Ryo has no limit. In the city only ryo can be packed; timber and stone come from the clan's towns (packs from several towns add up).

camp._note: War camp (Tim 2026-11-10). startWorkers = workers the camp begins with; more are hired at the camp for workerCost ryo each from the war chest, up to workerCap in all (training time as town workers). Camp workers gather only the resources listed (no food) anywhere in the war circle outside the town build ring, and drop at the camp hall into the camp stock, which no town ever sees. gatherSpeed = camp-only gather factor (1 = normal).

war._lineSnap: Tim 2026-11-15: a palisade run or a gate locks onto the end of a palisade or gate piece within this distance of the cursor.
war._resourceCampNote: 7c-4 placeholder, Tim to tune: a lumber camp or quarry may be placed outside the build area when a spot of its resource is within resourceCampReach; it does not extend the area.
war._buildersNote: 7c-4: builders now only limits a bot clan's camp (it still sends workers by itself). The player's camp workers build only where he sends them.
war._builderCapNote: Tim 2026-11-14: most workers a build order puts on one building site or hall upgrade (the nearest of those sent); repair and douse have no limit.
war._buildNote: Checkpoint 4, placeholders, Tim to tune. chainDistance = most distance from a new camp building to another camp building (centres). builders = most camp workers building one site at once. buildings: cost = timber and stone paid from the camp stock when placed; buildTicks = sim ticks of work for one worker (3 workers build 3 times as fast); radius = ground the building takes (spacing); max = most per camp; needs = built types first (upgrade = the camp hall upgrade); cap = troop cap each built one adds. hallUpgrade = the camp hall upgrade (ryo from the war chest), built by workers like a site. Palisade, gate and the second-special building come in later checkpoints.

maxByTier._note: Tim 2026-11-21: tents unlock with the war upgrade (no early rush): camp before / after the camp hall upgrade, town before / after the town hall war upgrade

heal._note: 7c placeholder, Tim to tune: the attacker's troops, hero and crew within radius of the finished clinic recover healFactor times faster (base recovery is units.json rules.regenPerSecond of full health a second, after regenAfterSeconds without being hit).

kennel._note: Checkpoint 7-3: clan = only that clan faction builds it. Trains the dog handler.
kennel._needsNote: Tim 2026-11-15: tier2 = a town hall at tier 2 or higher in a town, the camp hall upgrade in a camp

hidden_dojo._note: Checkpoint 7-5: Shinobi only. Trains the kunoichi.

camp_station._note: 8e-4 (2026-11-16), placeholders, Tim to tune: once built the camp lays its own rail spur to the nearest own town with a railway station (railways.link cost from the camp stores). Cost doubled by Tim 2026-11-17 (was 150 timber, 100 stone); a ruined station is rebuilt for the same cost.

stockade._note: Tim 2026-11-16: war camps build the stockade too (placeholders, Tim to tune). Troops go in up to buildings.stockade.garrison.capacity, heal like in a town stockade, ranged shoot out. Health: war.structures.campStockade by camp hall tier.

palisade._note: Checkpoint 6-6, placeholders, Tim to tune. Placed as a line: one piece every length along it (lineMax pieces at most in one run), cost and buildTicks per piece, thickness = how wide it blocks. A gate takes the place of a palisade piece (or stands alone) and lets only its own side through.
palisade._length: Tim 2026-11-15: pieces left gaps at length 5 (the art is drawn about 3.3 long at townArt._placedFootprint 0.6), so 3.2; cost, buildTicks, max and lineMax scaled to keep a run about the same price and time

gate._note: Tim 2026-11-15: a gate is two palisade pieces long (length 6.4, art drawn to match at townArt._placedFootprint 1.16): on a palisade it takes the place of two pieces, by the end of a run it locks onto the end, R turns it while placing.

armory._note: 8e-9 (Tim 2026-11-16), placeholders, Tim to tune: armory upgrades for one side of one war, troops only (not the hero or crew), gone when the war ends. Groups by war.units.<unit>.group (melee, ranged, mounted, siege), two tracks each: weapons = +step damage a level, armor = step less damage taken a level; levels per track; cost[level] = ryo from the war chest plus timber and stone from the camp or town stock; seconds per level while the armory stands; one in the work per side, up to queue in all (work included) paid when queued, a waiting one cancels for its full price (Tim 2026-11-18). No iron for now.

supply._note: 8e (2026-11-16), placeholders: treasuryKeep = default Clan treasury keep line for auto ryo orders (a clan sets its own); autoShare = share of the treasury above the keep line auto orders may take each game day; chestLow = a war chest below this gets an auto refill order of refill ryo (one open at a time).
supply._botCampKeepNote: placeholder (Tim 2026-11-17): a bot's town fills its own war camp's timber and stone orders down to this share of its storage (other orders, and a player's towns, keep the town's keep amount)
supply._sectionsNote: 8e-6: sections = marked rail sections on the camp spur inside the war circle (camp buildings on the camp morale bar); the line is cut while the camp station or any section is down. Tim 2026-11-17: the sections sit in a row just outside the camp: the first starts sectionStart along the track from the camp station, each is sectionLength long with sectionGap between, hit anywhere within sectionWidth of the red track (squeezed to fit a short stretch inside the war circle). The line opens again when all stand. A ruined station or section is rebuilt in place from its menu (station: its build cost; section: sectionCost, sectionBuildTicks of worker work), built by camp workers like a site. Camp ruins take no building slot (erase one to build on its spot). spurRefund = share of a torn-up spur cost that comes back to the town it ran to.

town._note: War checkpoint 8b (Tim 2026-11-15), placeholders, Tim to tune: the town hall war upgrade costs hallUpgrade.cost from town stock (ryo from the coffers), paid at once, at any tier; the town builders then build it (upgradeWork: each economy tick adds the number of builders, so 480 is 120 s with 4 builders), other projects wait while it is under way and it pauses while the hall is a ruin; it unlocks the military buildings that need upgrade. 8b-2: the defending town's military buildings (and its stable) train war.units into the defender war chest's troops only after musterSeconds from the declaration; trainSpeed multiplies how fast town queues train (1 = camp speed; a knob if prepared towns prove too strong). The defender war chest is filled from the town coffers (warChestTown) and goes back to them when the war ends.

standIn._note: Checkpoint 4 stand-in defender until the bot general (8d), placeholders: a bot clan's town at war trains one grunt every trainTicks for ryo from its coffers, up to max, hallDistance from the hall; they go for attacker units within the town ring + reach.

ranged._note: 7c-3b: every Nth stand-in troop is an archer that walks into the nearest house, workshop or farmhouse with room and shoots from it

dev._note: Dev build only: devStartWar gives the camp this pack when the attacker carries none.

structures._note: War checkpoint 6, placeholders, Tim to tune. Health of everything that stands in a war: townHall and campHall per tier (camp hall tier 2 = upgraded), town = placed town buildings by type (default for the rest; the stockade keeps buildings.stockade.garrison.hp), camp = war camp buildings by type, wall and gate per cell, zone = a grown house or workshop cell per stage. damage = factor on a unit's damage by attacker kind (siege = units with siege: true; none exist until checkpoint 7). fire: a melee hit sets a structure alight; it burns for damage health a second and dies lingerTicks after the last melee hit. searchRange = how far an attack-moving unit with no enemy to fight looks for a structure.

stone._note: Checkpoint 7-2: town structure types that resist fire bombs: bomb = factor on fire-bomb damage, and a bomb starts no fire on them.

structures._slotGapNote: 7c placeholder, Tim to tune: melee attackers of one clan on a structure each take their own spot round it, at least slotGap apart.

fire._note: 7c-2 placeholders, Tim to tune: only a finished Torch cast or a fire bomb lights it; one fire per structure. damage = health a second (the settled rule says about 8 to 10 grunts, near 150; kept lower until workers can douse and Tim has played it). burnTicks = sim ticks it burns, 0 = until workers douse it or the structure is a ruin.

repair._note: 7c-4 placeholders, Tim to tune: workers on a manual work order at their own structure. douseWork = worker ticks to put a fire out (60 = one worker 3 seconds, three workers 1 second). hpPerTick = health mended per worker per sim tick (building is faster). cost = timber and stone per health point from the town or camp stock. ruinShare = share of a ruined town hall's health in work before it stands again. botDousers = workers a bot clan sends to each of its fires by itself (stand-in until the bot general).

torch._note: 7c-2 placeholders, Tim to tune: castTicks = the torch cast at the structure (20 = 1 second); broken by stagger, stun, knockdown, charm and taunt, not by plain hits. types = unit types that can torch (every barracks unit: grunts, spearmen, brutes, enforcers; plain melee crew); a melee hero always can; riders, specials, ranged units and workers never.

zoneGarrison._note: 7c-3b placeholders, Tim to tune: the town owner's troops and crew can garrison these structure types (zone kinds housing and work, placed buildings house, workshop, farm), up to capacity each; units go in within range of it. Hits on them go to the building; melee inside cannot attack, ranged shoot out; no healing.
zoneGarrison._byType: Z4e placeholders, Tim to tune (2026-11-19: every tower and watchtower can be garrisoned): a watchtower holds 4 and its ranged troops reach 4 further

tower._note: Watchtower fire: a built watchtower shoots an arrow at the nearest enemy unit of its war within range, one every everyTicks sim ticks, for damage; speed = arrow speed. Camp watchtowers now; town watchtowers use the same numbers when towns get them (8b).
tower._sightNote: 7c placeholder, Tim to tune: a built watchtower lets its owner see units within sight of it, day and night.

shelter._note: Town hall shelter (Tim 2026-11-19: per worker): while a war is on a town, a worker with an attacker unit within nearRange of him or of his job spot runs to the town hall and stays inside (the others keep working); his load goes into the stores as he goes in. calmTicks = sim ticks with no attacker near him, his job spot or the hall before an automatic one goes back to work (sent in by hand: stays until Back to work); enterRange = how near the hall (in cells) counts as inside; capacityByTier = workers the hall holds by town hall tier (Camp, Village, Town).

units._note: War checkpoint 5 shared roster (Tim 2026-11-11 OK, enforcers at the barracks), placeholders, Tim to tune: ryo from the war chest per troop, trainTicks = sim ticks each (one at a time per building), at = camp buildings that train it, type = units.json type (one name, or one per clan faction), model = the body drawn per clan (stand-ins until the army kit art pass). War-only types (war_enforcer, army_archer, army_rifleman, sword_rider, mounted_pikeman) have no price in units.json, so they never show in a city hire menu. Checkpoint 7-1: clan = only that clan faction trains it (clan specials, special: true: their own look and abilities, at the clan hall).

grunt._note: 7c-2: the sword grunt of every clan (Kuroda's uses the swordsman body as a stand-in).

spearman._note: 7c-2 placeholder, Tim to tune: every clan trains a spearman at the barracks. Against its sword grunt: longer reach, more damage a second, a little less health (units.json spearman, shinobi_spearman). Yakuza and Shinobi use the Kuroda spearman body as a stand-in.

clanBonus._note: War checkpoint 5 placeholders, Tim to tune: per clan faction and roster unit, multipliers on ryo, trainTicks, hp and damage (missing = 1). Stat multipliers are set on each troop when it spawns.

cavalry._note: War checkpoint 5 placeholders, Tim to tune: a war.units entry with cavalry: true spawns already on a horse (horse = model per clan faction, hp = the rider's) and never gets off: no dismount on attack, hit or low health. It fights from the saddle at speed x its run speed. Rider and horse fall together.

founding._note: E1/E3 placeholders, Tim to tune. cost = ryo paid by the clan at founding; minSettlers must stand within gatherRadius of the hero; minSpacing = least distance to any other town or the capital (1600 from economy balance B4, Tim 2026-11-05: fewer, bigger towns; 600 rings never overlap); capitalSpacing = least distance to the capital point (Tim 2026-11-06: about 500 from the island gate, so a town can go up a short walk out); bots found only within botSiteRadius of a W1 site; startStock = what the settlers bring (no grind at the start); townHall is built at founding, firstProject is queued (unauthorized).
founding._placementNote: placeholder, Tim to tune: hall placement reach from hero and unit escape clearance in world units
founding._startWorkersNote: Tim 2026-11-05: free workers with every new town (on top of the settlers), in case there are no goods to train one

permit._note: E1 2026-11-05 placeholders, Tim to tune. A founding permit is bought at the Land Office (telegraph_office) and used up by the next founding. Player needs renown, crew and businesses held; bots need none of these (bots: false). ryo = permit price. maxTowns = towns a clan may found for now (C4 Influence raises it for the 2nd and 3rd town).
permit._townTierNote: Tim 2026-11-06: the Nth permit also needs one of your towns at this tier (2nd: Village, 3rd: Town); players only, like the other requirements

shinobi._note: Tim 2026-11-06: Shinobi hold no businesses, so they pay ryo instead

founding._graceNote: E1 2026-11-05: camp bandits leave a new town's people alone for this many days (inside graceRadius of the hall)

siteMenu._note: Choose-site menu at the island gate (E1): campWarn = warn when a bandit camp is this close to a site

rivalHints._note: Goals pass (Tim 2026-11-19), placeholders, Tim to tune: the Land Office talk on rival towns marks each rival's town (or the site it reserves for a rival not yet founded) with a question mark area on the World map. The mark's centre sits offsetMin to offsetMax from the town in a seeded direction, never on it; radius = the area drawn. Kept well inside discovery range so riding to the mark finds the town.

bots._note: E6 2026-11-05 placeholders, Tim to tune. Bots go once the player founds a first town, or by fallbackDay anyway. Departures are staggerDays apart per bot. Site score = traits (soil+water+defense) + clan taste - travel cost/travelScale + a seeded random roll up to randomRoll; a bot picks at random among the topPick best free sites. reserve = ryo kept back on top of permit, settlers and founding cost.
bots._leaveNote: Tim 2026-11-11: the first bot leaves afterPlayerDays after the player's first town (the next staggerDays later), or from fallbackDay if the player has no town by then. A Yakuza or Kuroda bot first holds minBusinesses, for at most businessWaitDays past its day. Bots save for the trip only from their day on.
bots._heroCrewNote: Tim 2026-11-17: a bot does not leave to found its town before its Hero group holds at least heroCrew standing crew (it takes the group along, 2026-11-06); while it is short it may hire.
bots._richNodeNote: Tim 2026-11-06: site score bonus per rich deposit within workers.range + campReach of the site

traits._note: Computed from the terrain round the spot (sim/frontier/founding.js siteTraits). soilWeight/defenseWeight = what each terrain code adds per sample (average over the circle), then soilShare/defenseShare = [level 2 from, level 3 from]; water = distance to the nearest river, lake or sea: waterNear = [level 3 up to, level 2 up to]; nodes counts resource nodes within nodeRadius.

_militaryBuildingsNote: War checkpoint 8b-1 (Tim 2026-11-15), placeholders, Tim to tune: military buildings a town builds inside its ring at any time, paid from town stock. Costs are the war camp costs (war.buildings); limits (max), needs and clan come from war.buildings, so both sides share them; needs upgrade = the town hall war upgrade (war.town). buildTicks are economy ticks of the town builders (the camp numbers / 20). No town hall tier limits. Ordinary placed-building upkeep (upkeep.buildings); unpaid upkeep only warns. The town stable is the existing stable.
_buildingCostNote: Tim 2026-11-05: placed building costs (storehouse, camps, stockade, market) doubled in economy pass 2

town_hall._note: E3 placeholder, Tim to tune: tier 1 town hall, built at founding (F6.1 grows it); houses the first settlers

house._note: F0.2: housing 6, cost 15 timber; buildTicks placeholder, Tim to tune

farm._note: F0.2: 0.03 food per worker per tick; cost and jobs placeholder, Tim to tune

lumber_camp._note: F0.2: 0.02 timber per worker per tick; cost and jobs placeholder, Tim to tune

food_camp._note: Tim 2026-11-07, placeholder, Tim to tune: fish and forage work camp (fishing grounds and fertile ground give food); same cart and storage rules as the lumber camp; art forage_camp from frontier sheet 3 (frbuilds3)

quarry._note: F0.2: 0.015 stone per worker per tick; cost and jobs placeholder, Tim to tune

workshop._note: F0.2: 1 timber + 0.5 stone into 1 goods every 40 sim ticks (2 economy ticks) with 2 workers; cost placeholder, Tim to tune

storehouse._note: placeholder, Tim to tune; no storage cap yet

stockade._costNote: Tim 2026-11-16: costByTier = what it costs by the town hall tier of its town (Village 400 timber and 450 stone, Town 500 and 600); cost = the fallback. sim/frontier/tiers.js buildingCost.
stockade._fortNote: Tim 2026-11-16: a fortress. hpByTier = full health by town hall tier (Village 40000, Town 60000; hp = the fallback). A town has up to tiers placed.stockade of them (0, 1, 3) and each holds capacity. War troops go in too (town stockades and the war camp stockade, war.buildings.stockade); every ranged unit inside shoots out during a war, reach further than from a house.
stockade._note: Tim 2026-11-06: 4-cell fort (size 2). garrison: your hero, crew and workers can shelter inside (capacity units), safe from attack and healing healFactor times faster; range = how close a unit must be to go in. hp (Tim 2026-11-06) = stockade health: hits on anyone inside go to the stockade; at 0 it is ruined and everyone piles out (enemies attacking the building itself waits for F7). Cost and times are placeholders, Tim to tune

capital._note: Tim 2026-11-07, placeholders to tune: the capital stable (the old rickshaw station art in the city) sells for clan ryo, no waiting, to a clan holding or having used a founding permit. What you buy waits on the island side of the gate. room: how many of each it adds to your stables' room.

room._note: Tim 2026-11-07: how many of each your stables can hold, by the town's tier (1, 2 Village, 3 Town); your limit is the sum over all your towns with a built stable. Owned ones are never taken away.

stable._note: Tim 2026-11-06/07, placeholders to tune: a placed building (no ryo costs). Horses, rickshaws and omnibuses are all made here by hand, one at a time on its production bar (seconds each, cost paid from town stock when queued, refunded on cancel); up to queue jobs wait on the bar and +5 queues five at once, up to the room its town's tier gives (stable.room); nothing is made on its own except one horse and one rickshaw for a bot clan. Click the stable or Space beside it opens the stable menu.

station._note: Tim 2026-11-06/07: omnibus station (coach house art), also the railway station (data/railways.json). Vehicles are made at the stable since 2026-11-07. reach: how close Space works; fightSeconds/enemyRange: no travel with a fight on.

infirmary._note: Tim 2026-11-06, placeholders to tune: your units within radius heal healFactor times faster; anyone knocked out on the island comes round at the nearest town's infirmary at full health (else at its hall at low health). One per Camp and Village, two per Town

market._note: Economy pass 2 D (Tim 2026-11-05): Village tier, 1 per town; sells goods above the town keep level for ryo (see market)
